nodes.title: This morning — one page
nodes.lede: A decision board built with NO per-document code: this node names the "decision-board" template and supplies only data. The engine assembles the primitives.

sections.heading: Ship the template layer?
sections.intro: Layer 2 renders a whole KIND of document from data. The question is whether to make it the default path for boards.

cards.lead: Every board becomes data, not a script.
paras: One template entry, authored once, serves every future board. Adding a new kind of document is adding a template — never writing a build_board.py.

cards.lead: Inline emphasis is the one caveat.
paras: Prose fields render through the safe rich subset (paragraphs, lists, links). Raw inline bold/code is escaped by design, so a migration that carried inline HTML loses that emphasis until a primitive opts into a richer inline op.

question.prompt: DECISION — make the template path the default for boards?

options.label: Yes — adopt it. Boards are data from here on.
Trial it on the next board, keep the bespoke path as fallback.
Let's talk about the inline-emphasis caveat first.

sections.heading: In flight — no decision needed
sections.intro: Shown so you can see it moving.

cards.lead: The expander ships zero new interpreter ops.
paras: It reuses the primitive interpreter's own path resolver and loop/condition semantics, so the assembly language and the render language are one.
